title.en: The Civil Rights Movement in Georgia

clips.send: Athens. Hunter and Holmes open UGA, January 1961. In January 1961 a federal judge ordered the University of Georgia to admit Charlayne Hunter and Hamilton Holmes, its first Black students. Governor Ernest Vandiver ordered the university closed, but a federal judge reversed that the next day. On January 18, 1961, Vandiver gave up “massive resistance” and backed the Sibley Commission’s plan; the legislature passed it on January 31. Hunter became a famous journalist; Holmes became a doctor.

clips.send: Savannah. Desegregation before the federal law. NAACP leader W. W. Law led protests and boycotts in Savannah. City leaders agreed to desegregate public and private facilities from October 1, 1963. That was about eight months before the federal Civil Rights Act of 1964.

clips.send: Atlanta. Auburn Avenue, SCLC, SNCC — and “too busy to hate”. Martin Luther King Jr. was born at 501 Auburn Avenue in 1929 and preached at Ebenezer Baptist Church with his father. The SCLC was founded here in 1957; SNCC made Atlanta its headquarters in October 1960. College students began the Atlanta Student Movement in 1960 with “An Appeal for Human Rights” and lunch-counter sit-ins. Atlanta’s public schools began to desegregate peacefully on August 30, 1961. Mayor Ivan Allen Jr. testified for the civil rights bill in Congress in 1963 — rare for a white Southern mayor.

clips.send: Columbus. One voter’s lawsuit opens the ballot box. Dr. Thomas Brewer recruited Primus King to try to vote in the July 4, 1944, Democratic primary. King was turned away. His lawsuit, King v. Chapman, struck down Georgia’s whites-only primary in 1945; the ruling was upheld in 1946. In one-party Georgia the Democratic primary decided who won, so this opened real voting power. Black voter registration jumped to about 125,000 within months.

clips.send: Albany. A whole community against segregation. SNCC field secretaries Charles Sherrod and Cordell Reagon came to register voters in 1961. In mid-November 1961 local groups united as the Albany Movement, with Dr. William G. Anderson as president. More than 1,000 people were jailed; Martin Luther King Jr. was arrested here in December 1961 and jailed again in 1962. Bernice Johnson Reagon and the SNCC Freedom Singers carried Albany’s freedom songs across the country.

clips.send: Americus. Young protesters face harsh charges. In 1963 student leaders in Americus were charged with “insurrection,” a crime that could carry the death penalty. They were later released — the case showed how far some officials would go to stop protests.

clips.send: 雅典城。亨特和霍姆斯打开了佐治亚大学的大门（1961 年 1 月）。1961 年 1 月，联邦法官命令佐治亚大学录取夏琳·亨特和汉密尔顿·霍姆斯，他们是该校第一批黑人学生。 万迪弗州长下令关闭大学，但第二天就被联邦法官推翻。 1961 年 1 月 18 日，万迪弗放弃“大规模抵制”，支持西布利委员会的方案；州议会于 1 月 31 日通过。 亨特后来成为著名记者，霍姆斯成为医生。

clips.send: 亚特兰大。奥本大道、SCLC、SNCC——以及“忙得没空去仇恨”。马丁·路德·金 1929 年出生在奥本大道 501 号，并和父亲一起在埃比尼泽浸信会教堂布道。 SCLC 于 1957 年在这里成立；SNCC 于 1960 年 10 月把总部设在亚特兰大。 1960 年，大学生发表《呼吁人权》并在午餐柜台静坐，开始了亚特兰大学生运动。 1961 年 8 月 30 日，亚特兰大公立学校开始和平地取消种族隔离。 1963 年，小伊万·艾伦市长到国会作证支持民权法案——这在南方白人市长中十分罕见。

clips.send: 奥尔巴尼。整个社区一起反对种族隔离。1961 年，SNCC 外勤干事查尔斯·谢罗德和科德尔·里根来到这里登记选民。 1961 年 11 月中旬，当地组织联合成立奥尔巴尼运动，推选威廉·安德森医生为主席。 一千多人被捕；马丁·路德·金 1961 年 12 月在这里被捕，1962 年再次入狱。 伯妮斯·约翰逊·里根和 SNCC 自由歌手把奥尔巴尼的自由之歌带到了全国。

clips.send: 哥伦布。一位选民的诉讼打开了投票箱。托马斯·布鲁尔医生请普里默斯·金去参加 1944 年 7 月 4 日的民主党初选投票，金被拒之门外。 他的诉讼“金诉查普曼案”在 1945 年推翻了佐治亚州只允许白人参加的初选，1946 年该判决被维持。 在一党独大的佐治亚州，民主党初选决定谁当选，所以这一判决打开了真正的投票权。 几个月内，黑人选民登记人数猛增到约 12.5 万人。
